items.followUp: What is the role of the cell plate during cytokinesis in plant cells?

rubric.why: Identifies the structure formed by the phragmoplast.
rubric.description: Names the cell plate or new cell wall formed during plant-cell division.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the cell plate or the new wall formed between daughter cells.

rubric.why: States the phragmoplast’s role in separating the daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains that the phragmoplast helps divide the plant cell during cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Award for linking its role to cytokinesis or separation of the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast is a structure of microtubules that forms between the two daughter nuclei during plant-cell division.
It guides the formation of a cell plate, which develops into a new cell wall and separates the daughter cells.

items.followUp: What is meant by an enzyme-substrate complex?

rubric.why: Defines the active site through its interaction with the substrate.
rubric.description: States that the active site is the region of an enzyme where the substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the active site as the enzyme’s substrate-binding region.

rubric.why: Gives the two functions of the active site.
rubric.description: States that the active site binds the substrate and is where the reaction is catalysed.
rubric.how: Award when both substrate binding and catalysis or product formation are conveyed.

modelAnswer: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
It binds the substrate and catalyses its conversion into product.

items.followUp: What happens to electrons during oxidation and reduction?

rubric.why: Identifies a defining feature of oxidation.
rubric.description: Oxidation involves gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, or loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award for any one correct defining feature of oxidation.

rubric.why: Identifies a defining feature of reduction.
rubric.description: Reduction involves loss of oxygen, gain of hydrogen, or gain of electrons.
rubric.how: Award for any one correct defining feature of reduction.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, or loss of electrons.
Reduction is the loss of oxygen, gain of hydrogen, or gain of electrons.

items.followUp: Name two factors that can limit the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Explains that a limiting factor affects the rate of a process.
rubric.description: Defines limiting factors as factors that influence or restrict the rate of a process.
rubric.how: Award for linking a factor to the rate of a biological process.

rubric.why: States how a factor becomes limiting.
rubric.description: Explains that the factor in shortest supply restricts the rate.
rubric.how: Award for stating that shortage or limited availability limits the rate.

modelAnswer: Limiting factors are factors that affect the rate of a biological process.
The factor that is in the shortest supply restricts the rate of that process.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Names the raw materials and the food made in photosynthesis.
rubric.description: States that plants use carbon dioxide and water to make glucose or food.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying the raw materials and product.

rubric.why: Includes the conditions and oxygen release.
rubric.description: States that the process occurs using light energy and chlorophyll, with oxygen released.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning light and chlorophyll and the release of oxygen.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy, absorbed by chlorophyll, to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
Oxygen is released during the process.

items.followUp: What is one structural difference between saturated and unsaturated fats?

rubric.why: States the defining bond feature of saturated fatty acids.
rubric.description: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that saturated fatty acids contain no double bonds.

rubric.why: States the defining bond feature of unsaturated fatty acids.
rubric.description: Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that unsaturated fatty acids contain at least one double bond.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds.
Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-carbon double bonds.

items.followUp: How does transpiration help cool a plant?

rubric.why: Identifies the harmful effect of excessive transpiration.
rubric.description: States that excessive transpiration causes too much water to be lost from the plant.
rubric.how: Award for identifying harmful water loss.

rubric.why: States a consequence of excessive water loss.
rubric.description: Explains that excessive water loss can cause wilting, dehydration, or death.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least one resulting harm.

modelAnswer: Transpiration may be harmful when water is lost faster than the roots can replace it.
Excessive water loss causes wilting and, in severe cases, may lead to the death of the plant.

items.followUp: Explain four more careers related to Biology.

rubric.why: Provides a biology-related career and its contribution.
rubric.description: Medicine: uses biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent, or treat disease.
rubric.how: Award for a correct explanation of medicine or a medical profession.

rubric.why: Provides a second distinct biology-related career and its contribution.
rubric.description: Agriculture: applies biology to improve crops, livestock, or food production.
rubric.how: Award for a correct explanation of agriculture.

rubric.why: Provides a third distinct biology-related career and its contribution.
rubric.description: Fisheries: applies biology to fish breeding, fish farming, or management of fish resources.
rubric.how: Award for a correct explanation of fisheries or aquaculture.

rubric.why: Provides a fourth distinct biology-related career and its contribution.
rubric.description: Forestry: applies biology to the management and conservation of forests and trees.
rubric.how: Award for a correct explanation of forestry.

modelAnswer: Medicine: Medical professionals use biology to understand the human body, diagnose diseases, and treat patients.
Agriculture: Agricultural scientists use biology to improve crops and livestock and increase food production.
Fisheries: Fisheries specialists use biology to breed and rear fish and manage fish resources.
Forestry: Foresters use biological knowledge to manage and conserve forests and their resources.
